messages:
anais: Heads up — saw a bunch of 30s cold-start spikes hitting /v1/generate in prod tonight (eu-west-1). P95 stayed ok but p99 blew out on a few routes. Anyone else seeing aggressive node termination?

leo: saw the same alerts, p99 jumped from ~2s -> ~26s around 02:13 UTC. cluster-autoscaler ScaleDown events spiked, then a flurry of PodPreemption/Terminate.

mira: Looking at node events — kubelet reported transient volume attach delays, then CA considered the node underutilized and scaled down. Prewarmed GPU cache didn't survive the pod move. Might be probe jitter + eviction timing.

taylor: Quick thought: our current downscale cooldown is 2m and we have probe_period_seconds=10 with aggressive failureThreshold=1. That combo is pretty sensitive to transient flakiness. I'd rather widen hysteresis than raise min nodes.

sami: Agree. Two levers: lengthen scale-down-unneeded-duration + add a short maintenance window for standby pools so we don't nuked nodes right after a restore. Cost estimate: bumping min nodes by 1 in eu-west-1 is ~+$55/day.

anais: Noted. We need to balance SLO vs cost. The routes impacted have 99 SLO at 10s. If we add a 3m unneeded-duration, we probably kill fewer prewarm-resources.

leo: Also saw a pattern where pods with initContainers for GPU cache fail readiness for ~20s on node move. Maybe add an annotation to mark these as "preserve-on-drain" so CA respects them?

mira: We can use a PodDisruptionBudget, but PDB prevents drains, not scale-to-zero decisions. CA ignores PDBs in some configs. Instead, how about marking the DaemonSet + prewarm pods with nodeAffinity to keep them on standby nodes and only evict when capacity needed?

taylor: Prototype annotation we tested in staging:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-prewarm
  annotations:
    redwood.com/standby-preserve: "true"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: prewarm
    image: redwood/prewarm:stable
```

We patched CA to treat that annotation as a "do-not-scale-down-until: 5m" hint. Works in staging but needs CA extension.

infra-bot: [autoscaler] ScaleDown: node/i-08a3 removed from pool-gpu-eu-2 (reason: utilization<0.15) at 2026-03-11T02:13:47Z

sami: If extending cooldowns, we should add a cheap predictive signal too — if recent traffic ramp happened within last 10m, hold nodes. Could use request-rate lookback on the ingress metrics.

anais: Good idea. Add ramp-detection + short hold window. Implementation plan: (1) increase scaleDown.unneededDuration -> 3m; (2) add CA webhook to respect redwood.com/standby-preserve annotation for 5m; (3) instrument ingress ramp metric and short-circuit scale-down when ramp>threshold.

leo: SGTM. I'll open a PR for the CA webhook and an infra playbook change. Also will run a cost calc on keeping one extra standby in eu-west-1 vs the risk of SLA penalties.

mira: I'll adjust kubelet probe settings for prewarm pods to be less aggressive (failureThreshold 3, period 10s). Should reduce false positives during attach delays.

taylor: We should also add a post-scale audit that logs how many prewarm pods were moved by scale-down in the last hour so we can tune.

anais: Thanks all. Can someone own the PR + quick telemetry dashboard? Prefer not to leave this as a manual ops change. @leo + @mira?

leo: I'll take the PR. Will link to it here when ready. :+1:

mira: I'll do the dashboard and probe change, and run a canary in eu-west-1 for 24h.

infra-bot: [alert] Latency SLO: route=/v1/generate p99 exceeded 10s (26.3s) — triggered at 2026-03-11T02:14:12Z

sami: Ping if we see recurrence after the canary; if so we should consider a small reserved standby pool in the busiest regions.

anais: Sounds good. I'll update customer-facing incident notes and include the mitigation plan.
